ventral_fluke_pixel_intensity_distributi.global_contrast_ratio: High-contrast distribution with approximately 75% low-intensity (black/dark grey) pixels and 25% high-intensity (white) pixels primarily located at the distal tips and along the trailing edge.
ventral_fluke_pixel_intensity_distributi.spatial_color_mapping: Central and lower fluke regions are characterized by a solid dark contiguous mass. High-contrast white mottling and contiguous white patches are mapped to the upper 20% of the fluke area, extending from the median notch to the distal tips on both lobes.

trailing_edge_2d_geometric_contour.median_notch_angle: Deep V-shaped median notch with an estimated pixel angle of 55-65 degrees and a bounding-box depth approximately 1/8th of the vertical fluke height.
trailing_edge_2d_geometric_contour.edge_topography_serration_map: High-frequency, irregular serration pattern along the entire trailing edge. Visible peaks and valleys range from 5 to 15 pixels in amplitude, with the highest concentration of jagged peaks occurring on the inner trailing edge of both lobes.
trailing_edge_2d_geometric_contour.lobe_sweep_trajectory: Bi-lateral convex curvature on the outer margins, transitioning to a slight concave curve as the trailing edge approaches the median notch.

localized_surface_anomalies.rosette_scar_constellations: Dense clusters of circular, high-contrast white and beige pixel aggregates (barnacle colonies) are localized on the extreme distal tips (left and right) of the fluke.
localized_surface_anomalies.linear_abrasions: Distinct dark vertical linear disruptions (rake marks) are visible against the white pigmented background of the upper right lobe, oriented roughly perpendicular to the trailing edge.

acquired_anomalies_or_scars: Extensive barnacle colonization on the distal tips and visible parallel rake marks on the right lobe's ventral surface.
other_distinctive_markers: Unique asymmetric pigmentation pattern where the right lobe contains a significantly larger and more contiguous white patch compared to the more fragmented mottling on the left lobe.
